# scrumit

> scrumit is a local-first console for sprints, kanban boards and epics where the
> artefacts are plain markdown files with YAML front-matter, versioned with git.
> The repository is the database. This file is the complete specification of that
> format, written so that a language model can create and move work by editing
> files directly — no app, no API, no network.

An agent that can read and write files needs nothing else. Every operation below
is a file edit. Nothing is stored outside the repository, and nothing in the
repository depends on scrumit continuing to exist.

---

## 1. Invariants

These are the rules that keep the format honest. Violating any of them produces
either a file a human cannot read or a diff a reviewer cannot trust.

**MUST**

- Write YAML front-matter as the very first thing in the file, delimited by
  exactly `---` on its own line, opening and closing.
- Keep `id` stable forever. It is the primary key, it appears in `blocked_by`,
  `epic` and sprint references, and other people's commit messages.
- Write dates as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. No times, no timezones, no local formats.
- Derive the file path from the artefact's own fields (§5). The fields win.
- Put a markdown file's `id` in front-matter before anything can reference it.
- Set `updated` to today's date whenever you change an issue.
- Preserve every front-matter key you do not understand, verbatim.

**MUST NOT**

- Reformat, reflow or re-indent the markdown body. Change only what you were
  asked to change. A rewrite that touches prose is a defect, not a tidy-up.
- Renumber or reuse ids. A new issue takes the next number up; a deleted issue's
  number is retired.
- Invent enum values. `status` and `type` accept the five and four values below
  and nothing else.
- Create a second file for the same `id`. If one exists, edit it.
- Touch `.git/`. scrumit reads `.git/HEAD` and never writes to it.
- Add build output, caches or `node_modules` paths to the artefacts.

**GOOD TO KNOW**

- If the folder a file sits in disagrees with its front-matter, the front-matter
  wins. scrumit will move the file the next time it writes it. Keep the tree
  tidy by moving it yourself (see §6).
- Any `.md` file anywhere in the repository with an `id` key is a card. Without
  an `id` it is documentation and is ignored, so `README.md` beside your issues
  is fine.
- Front-matter keys scrumit does not recognise are carried through every write
  untouched, so you can safely add `jira:`, `okr:` or anything else.

## 2. Directory layout

Every path is configurable in `.scrumit/config.yaml`; these are the defaults.

```
repo-root/
  .scrumit/
    config.yaml                    # board columns, directories, settings
    AGENTS.md                      # this specification, generated per repo
    templates/                     # optional starting points for new issues
  backlog/
    ACME-118.md                    # no sprint yet
  sprints/
    2026-S20/
      sprint.md                    # goal, dates, capacity, retrospective
      ACME-140.md
  epics/
    EPIC-01-checkout-reliability.md
  done/
    2026-S19/                      # finished work, archived by sprint
      ACME-120.md
    ACME-161.md                    # finished with no sprint
```

Everything under `.git/`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `out/`, `vendor/`,
`coverage/`, `target/`, `.next/`, `.turbo/` and `.venv/` is skipped when
scanning.

## 3. Issue file

```markdown
---
id: ACME-140
title: Retry webhook delivery with backoff
status: doing
type: story
epic: EPIC-01
sprint: 2026-S20
points: 3
assignee: tobias-rehn
priority: 1
labels:
  - reliability
blocked_by:
  - ACME-138
created: 2026-10-14
updated: 2026-10-16
order: 20
---

## Context

Webhook consumers see duplicate deliveries when a 5xx is followed by a slow
recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retry at 1s, 8s, 60s, then dead-letter
- [ ] Duplicate deliveries drop below 0.01%
```

### Front-matter reference

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | **yes** | — | `PREFIX-N`, uppercase. Stable forever. See §6 for how to pick the next one. |
| `title` | string | no | first heading, else `id` | One line, sentence case, no trailing period. |
| `status` | enum | no | `backlog` | `backlog` `todo` `doing` `review` `done` |
| `type` | enum | no | `story` | `story` `bug` `chore` `spike` |
| `epic` | string \| null | no | null | An epic `id`, e.g. `EPIC-01`. |
| `sprint` | string \| null | no | null | A sprint `id`, which is also the folder name. |
| `points` | number | no | null | Estimate. Integer or half, never hours. |
| `assignee` | string | no | null | Handle, lowercase hyphenated: `ana-marin`. |
| `priority` | 0–3 | no | null | `0` drop everything, `1` this sprint, `2` next, `3` someday. |
| `labels` | string[] | no | `[]` | Free-form, lowercase. |
| `blocked_by` | string[] | no | `[]` | Issue ids. A card is *blocked* while any listed id is not `done`. |
| `links` | string[] | no | `[]` | URLs. |
| `order` | number | no | `0` | Manual position within the column. Lower sorts first. |
| `created` | date | no | null | Set once. |
| `updated` | date | no | null | Set on every change. |

Omit a key rather than writing `null`, `""` or `[]`. A file written by hand
should look like a file a person wrote.

### Body conventions

The body is free markdown and scrumit never rewrites it. Two conventions earn
their keep:

- `## Context` — why this exists, in a paragraph or two.
- `## Acceptance criteria` — a task list. scrumit counts `- [ ]` and `- [x]` and
  shows `2/5` on the card and in the editor, and the Flow view reports started
  issues that have no checklist at all.

## 4. Epic and sprint files

### Epic

```markdown
---
id: EPIC-01
title: Checkout reliability
state: active
owner: lise-okafor
target: 2026-12-15
color: 1
---

Every path from authorisation to settlement should be idempotent and
reconcilable. If a payment fails, the merchant should find out why without
asking us.
```

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | **required** | Conventionally `EPIC-NN`. |
| `title` | string | first heading | |
| `state` | enum | `planned` | `planned` `active` `done` |
| `owner` | string | null | |
| `target` | date | null | |
| `color` | 1–8 | derived from the id | Indexes the theme's hue ramp, so an epic keeps its colour family across themes. |

Epic progress is never stored. It is the sum of its issues.

### Sprint

```markdown
---
id: 2026-S20
name: Sprint 20
state: active
goal: Make webhook delivery trustworthy end to end.
start: 2026-10-15
end: 2026-10-28
capacity: 34
---

## Working agreements

- Wednesday is integration day
```

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | parent folder name | Conventionally `YYYY-SNN`. Doubles as the folder. |
| `name` | string | the id | |
| `state` | enum | `planned` | `planned` `active` `closed` |
| `goal` | string | `""` | One sentence a stakeholder would understand. |
| `start` / `end` | date | null | Drives days-remaining and the burndown. |
| `capacity` | number | null | Committed points. Exceeding it is reported, not blocked. |

A sprint folder with issues but no `sprint.md` is legal: scrumit shows the
sprint and marks it as having no file yet. Write the `sprint.md` when you have
a goal, dates or a retro to record.

## 5. Path derivation

The path is a function of the fields. This is what makes a hand-moved file and a
hand-edited field converge on the same place.

```
status == done and sprint set   ->  done/<sprint>/<id>.md
status == done and no sprint    ->  done/<id>.md
sprint set                      ->  sprints/<sprint>/<id>.md
otherwise                       ->  backlog/<id>.md

epic                            ->  epics/<EPIC-ID>-<slug(title)>.md
sprint                          ->  sprints/<sprint-id>/sprint.md
config                          ->  .scrumit/config.yaml
```

`<slug>` is the title lowercased, accents folded to ASCII, runs of non-letters
replaced by `-`, truncated to 48 characters. An epic's file name is fixed when it
is created: retitling an epic does not move its file.

## 6. Operations

Every recipe below is a complete description of the file changes involved.

### Create an issue

1. Choose the id: reuse the prefix already in use in this repository and take the
   highest `<PREFIX>-N` for that prefix, plus one. If the repository has no issues
   yet, derive the prefix from the first word of the project name
   (`Acme Payments Platform` → `ACME`), or use `SCRUM` when there is no project
   name. Never mix prefixes within one repository.
2. Choose the path from §5. A new, unscheduled issue goes in `backlog/`.
3. Set `order` to the highest `order` in the target column plus 10. If the column
   is empty, use `10`.
4. Set `created` and `updated` to today.
5. Write the file. Keep it short: title, and a body with `## Context` and
   `## Acceptance criteria` when you know them.

```sh
# The smallest useful card.
cat > backlog/ACME-150.md <<'EOF'
---
id: ACME-150
title: Reject duplicate refund requests
status: backlog
type: bug
points: null
labels:
  - payments
created: 2026-10-16
updated: 2026-10-16
order: 10
---

## Context

A client retry after a timeout can refund twice.
EOF
```

### Move an issue to another column

Edit `status`, set `updated`, and move the file to the path §5 now derives.

```sh
sed -i '' 's/^status: todo$/status: doing/' sprints/2026-S20/ACME-140.md
git mv sprints/2026-S20/ACME-140.md sprints/2026-S20/ACME-140.md   # no move needed
```

The move is only needed when `sprint` or `done` changes the directory. Changing
`status` within a sprint's directory does not move anything.

### Schedule an issue into a sprint

Set `sprint` to the sprint id and move the file from `backlog/` to
`sprints/<sprint>/`.

### Complete an issue

Set `status: done`. If it belongs to a sprint, the file moves to
`done/<sprint>/`; if not, to `done/`. Do this rather than deleting: the archive
is what makes velocity, throughput and lead time computable.

### Close a sprint

Set `state: closed` in `sprints/<id>/sprint.md`. Unfinished issues stay in place
unless you also move them: return them to `backlog/` and set `sprint: null`, or
carry them into the next sprint by setting `sprint` to its id. Record what you
learned in the body under `## Retro`.

### Create an epic

Pick the next `EPIC-NN`, choose a `color` from 1–8 that no active epic is using,
and write `epics/EPIC-NN-<slug>.md`.

### Reprioritise

Change `priority`, or `order` within a column. Do not renumber every card: leave
gaps. scrumit spaces by 10 precisely so a single drop rewrites a single file.

### Bulk edit

Apply the same field edit across files, then set `updated` on each. A
one-property change across twenty issues should read as twenty one-line diffs.

## 7. config.yaml

```yaml
version: 1
project: Acme Payments Platform
columns:
  - { id: backlog, name: Backlog, wip: null }
  - { id: todo,    name: To do,   wip: null }
  - { id: doing,   name: Doing,   wip: 3 }
  - { id: review,  name: Review,  wip: 4 }
  - { id: done,    name: Done,    wip: null, terminal: true }
backlog:  { dir: backlog }
sprints:  { dir: sprints, length_days: 14 }
epics:    { dir: epics }
archive:  { dir: done }
ceremony: Planning Monday, review and retro every second Friday
vocabulary: { points: true, assignees: true, priorities: true }
```

Those are the real defaults. A limit on `To do` is a legitimate thing to add if
you want to police the sprint commitment, but it is not one out of the box —
work-in-progress limits belong on the columns where work is actually in progress.

- Column **ids are fixed** to the five statuses, because status decides which
  folder a file lives in and that has to be portable between people and machines.
  Rename, reorder, cap and hide freely; do not invent an id.
- `wip` is a work-in-progress ceiling. Exceeding it is reported on the board and
  in the Flow view, and blocks nothing.
- `terminal: true` marks the column excluded from cycle-time and flow maths.
- Every `dir` is relative to the repository root.
- A missing config is fine: the defaults above apply.

## 8. Before you finish

- [ ] `id` unique across the repository, and nothing renumbered.
- [ ] Path matches §5 for the artefact's own fields.
- [ ] `updated` is today's date on every issue you touched.
- [ ] The markdown body is unchanged unless changing it was the point.
- [ ] Front-matter you did not need is still there, byte for byte.
- [ ] `status` and `type` are values from the enum tables, exactly.
- [ ] No file was created that duplicates an existing `id`.
- [ ] `git status` shows what you expect: one file per logical change.

## 9. Reading the result back

In Chrome and Edge, scrumit watches the repository and rebuilds the board within
about a second of a file changing, so work you do is visible without anyone
asking for a reload. In other browsers it caches an index and needs a nudge:
press **Rescan** in the top bar, or just reopen the repository. Either way the
format is identical.

One asymmetry is worth knowing. On its next write, scrumit puts a card back at
the path §5 derives, so drift is corrected rather than reported. A careless path
will be quietly tidied instead of flagged. Get the path right, and let the test
suite tell you if you have not.

`git` remains yours. scrumit reads the branch name from `.git/HEAD` and makes no
attempt at `git status`, so commit, branch and merge in the terminal. A branch
switch shows up on the board on its own.

## 10. Running scrumit

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5178
npm run check      # typecheck, then the format, adapter and spec tests
npm run smoke      # drive a real browser, screenshot every view
```

Opening a folder uses the File System Access API, so it needs Chrome or Edge.
Everything works in the bundled demo repository otherwise. Use
**Settings → AI agents** to write this specification into a repository as
`.scrumit/AGENTS.md`.
